newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian government plans to give away the Queen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian government plans to give away the Queen.

text.p: As Australia debates whether to keep Britain's Queen Elizabeth as head of state or become a republic, the conservative government of Prime Minister John Howard has decided to give the queen away - or at least her portrait.
The government will now give away free photographic portraits of the Queen to anyone who asks, Administrative Services Minister David Jull said on Friday.
Jull told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio there had been a lot of requests for pictures of the Queen in recent months and he believed there was still a large untapped market.
"Once it is known that the portraits are available I am sure that the consumption will increase dramatically," he said.
Government bookshops sold portraits of Queen Elizabeth until 1992 when the former Labor government of republican Prime Minister Paul Keating took them off the shelves because of a lack of demand.

Australians will vote before the turn of the century on whether to keep the British monarch as head of state or become a republic. Opinion polls generally show half or just half of Australians favour becoming a republic.
